## Not Just Your Agent, Your Advocate

I'm Brian Butler with eXp Realty (License SA701819000), and I specialize in San Tan Valley and Florence real estate. 4 years licensed in Arizona real estate, focused exclusively on San Tan Valley and Florence.

If you're buying or selling in San Tan Valley or Florence, I know these markets cold. I know the difference between communities like Pecan Creek and Johnson Ranch, what land parcels in Florence actually make sense, which builders consistently deliver quality, and what homes are priced right versus what's been sitting too long.

Most of my clients are first-time buyers or people relocating to Arizona who want straight answers. No pressure, no sales pitch, no rushing you into decisions you're not ready for.

What I believe in: showing you exactly what you're buying, explaining what it means for your money, and fighting hard for you during negotiations. My job is to make sure you understand the San Tan Valley and Florence markets -- not just get you to sign paperwork.

One of my favorite parts of this job is handing first-time buyers the keys to their new home and watching their face light up. That moment never gets old.

Whether you're buying your first home in San Tan Valley, selling your property in Florence, or just have questions about these markets -- let's talk. No agenda. Just honest answers from someone who actually knows these areas.

I will never push you toward a house you're not sure about. I will never rush your timeline. And I will always give you the honest truth about a property -- good and bad.

## My Approach to Selling Your Home

Selling your home is one of the biggest financial decisions you'll make. You deserve an agent who tells you the truth, markets aggressively, and keeps you informed every single week. It starts with a detailed CMA (Comparative Market Analysis) so you know exactly where you stand.

I'd rather tell you a price you don't love and sell your home in 30 days than tell you what you want to hear and watch it sit for months. That's how I operate.

## My Marketing Plan

- Professional photography and video tour

- Targeted social media marketing to active buyers

- MLS listing with syndication to Zillow, Realtor.com, Redfin, and 100+ sites

- Direct outreach to agents with active buyers in your price range

- Strategic open houses to create urgency

- Weekly updates with showing feedback and market data

- Skilled negotiation to maximize your net proceeds

- Full transaction management from listing to closing

Neighborhood Guides

## Know the Neighborhoods, Not Just the City

Two homes five minutes apart can be very different purchases. Each guide covers the homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs nobody puts in the listing.

### San Tan Valley neighborhoods San Tan Valley overview ->

### Johnson Ranch

Johnson Ranch in San Tan Valley -- 2,000 acres, golf, three rec centers, Hunt Highway living. Homes, schools, HOA and tradeoffs, plainly explained.

### Solera at Johnson Ranch

Solera at Johnson Ranch is a gated Del Webb 55-plus community of 727 homes inside Johnson Ranch, with its own clubhouse and the Johnson Ranch golf course through it.

### Encanterra

Encanterra by Shea Homes -- a gated Trilogy resort community in San Tan Valley with La Casa club, Tom Lehman golf, all-ages and 55-plus sections.

### Pecan Creek

Pecan Creek in northern San Tan Valley -- J.O. Combs schools inside the neighborhood, four main parks, and one of the shorter drives to Queen Creek and the Loop 202.

### San Tan Heights

San Tan Heights -- a large foothills community in western San Tan Valley with mountain views, miles of trails, and San Tan Heights Elementary inside the community.

### Copper Basin

Copper Basin is an 847-acre village-center community in San Tan Valley with its own YMCA, Copper Basin Elementary, fire station, and 20-acre park on Main Street.

### Ironwood Crossing

Ironwood Crossing by Fulton Homes at Ironwood and Ocotillo -- aquatics center with a 7,000 sq ft heated pool, 20 parks, and a charter school inside the community.

### Circle Cross Ranch

Circle Cross Ranch in San Tan Valley -- a Florence Unified elementary school and Empire Park inside the community, walking trails, and one of the closer drives to Queen Creek, Gilbert and Mesa.

### Skyline Ranch

Skyline Ranch at the base of the San Tan Mountains -- Mediterranean-style homes, Skyline Ranch Elementary, and the gated acre-lot enclave of Encanto Real.

### Rancho Bella Vista

Rancho Bella Vista and Rancho Bella Vista South -- 2003-2009 homes between Hunt Highway and Gantzel, surrounded by farmland, with mountain views and a lower-profile HOA.

### Florence neighborhoods Florence overview ->

### Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Parkside

Parkside at Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- the all-ages side of Florence's Merrill Ranch master plan, with the community park, water amenities, and Poston Butte golf.

### Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch

Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Florence's 55-plus section of Merrill Ranch, with a 48,000 sq ft clubhouse, Poston Butte golf, and access to the wider Merrill Ranch amenities.

### Florence Gardens

Florence Gardens is an established 55-plus community in Florence where homeowners own their land -- 1,219 lots, clubhouse, pools, pickleball, and a 9-hole executive golf course, with no lot rent.

### Historic Downtown Florence

Living in and around historic Florence -- Main Street, the 1891 Pinal County Courthouse, McFarland State Historic Park, historic homes, and the original town subdivisions.

### Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor

Florence's active building corridor -- Magma Ranch and Magma Ranch Vistas, Magic Ranch, and the newer subdivisions west of town, with Magma Ranch Elementary and new-home buying guidance.

### Florence Land Parcels

Florence, AZ

Florence offers land parcel opportunities that have largely disappeared from closer-in markets. If you're looking to build, invest in raw land, or want acreage at a price that makes sense -- Florence is worth a serious look.

TypeResidential lots & raw land

Best ForBuilders, investors, acreage buyers

## PAGE: San Tan Valley Neighborhoods — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley

## San Tan Valley, Arizona Neighborhoods

A plain guide to the neighborhoods • Homes, schools, commutes, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley

## Start here

San Tan Valley sits south of Queen Creek and north of Florence, against the San Tan Mountains. For years people described it as the unincorporated part of Pinal County south of Queen Creek. That description is out of date.

Residents voted to incorporate on August 5, 2025. Pinal County approved the incorporation on September 17, 2025, and the new Town of San Tan Valley took over services that the county used to run on July 1, 2026. It is Arizona's 92nd municipality and, with more than 100,000 residents, the largest community ever to incorporate in the state. Town hall is at the San Tan Valley County Complex on Schnepf Road, and town services are still being built out. When you buy here, ask who currently provides the service at that address today, not who provided it two years ago.

Most of San Tan Valley is master-planned subdivisions built from the late 1990s through today, plus acre and half-acre ranchette pockets on the edges. That mix is the whole decision. Two homes five minutes apart can be very different purchases: one in an HOA with a community pool and a school in the subdivision, the next on a well and septic with horse privileges and no HOA at all.

## The question that decides the search

When buyers sit down with me, I ask for the one thing the house has to do for them. In San Tan Valley that answer usually sorts the neighborhoods faster than price does:

- Golf, pools, and a lot of organized activity inside the neighborhood: Johnson Ranch, and its 55-plus enclave Solera.

- Resort-level amenities and a private club, with a budget to match: Encanterra.

- A school and a park inside the subdivision so most days stay close to home: Pecan Creek, Copper Basin, Ironwood Crossing, Circle Cross Ranch, San Tan Heights.

- More house and more lot for the money, accepting a longer drive to the 202: Skyline Ranch, Rancho Bella Vista, and the southern Hunt Highway corridor.

- No HOA, room for trailers, shops, and animals: the ranchette pockets off the main subdivisions. These are found street by street, not as named communities, and they need a different kind of diligence on wells, septic, flood plain, and road maintenance.

If you are selling here, the same sorting matters in reverse. Your buyer is comparing you to new construction a mile away with builder incentives. Pricing and condition need to answer that comparison directly, with numbers in front of the buyer, not adjectives.

## Quick facts: San Tan Valley as a whole

- Location: Northern Pinal County, roughly 45 to 55 minutes to central Phoenix depending on where in the valley you start and which route is moving.

- ZIP codes you will see on listings: 85140, 85142, 85143, 85144. A Queen Creek mailing address does not always mean Town of Queen Creek services. Check the parcel, not the envelope.

- Main corridors: Hunt Highway north-south, Ironwood/Gantzel north-south, Combs Road and Ocotillo Road east-west, Bella Vista Road in the south.

- Freeway access: Loop 202 via Ironwood and via State Route 24. This is the pressure point of the area. Drives are reasonable off-peak and slow at school and commute hours on Ironwood and Hunt Highway.

- Schools: Two districts. J.O. Combs Unified serves the northern part (Combs High School, Combs Middle School, Harmon, Ellsworth, Ranch and Simonton elementary schools). Florence Unified serves most of the rest (Poston Butte High School, San Tan Foothills High School, Walker Butte and San Tan Mountain middle schools, and elementary schools inside Copper Basin, Circle Cross Ranch, San Tan Heights, Skyline Ranch, and others). Charter options include American Leadership Academy and Legacy Traditional campuses in the valley.

- Hospitals and care: Banner Ironwood Medical Center on Combs Road, plus urgent care clinics on Ironwood and in Queen Creek. Florence Hospital serves the south end.

- Outdoor anchor: San Tan Mountain Regional Park, more than 10,000 acres of trails on the west side. This is the amenity that does not show up in a listing photo and matters on a Saturday.

- Library and town services: San Tan Valley Library on Schnepf Road (opened 2021), now part of the new town's service build-out.

## Tradeoffs nobody puts in the listing

- Commute. Price per square foot drops as you go south and east for a reason. Drive your actual commute at your actual time before you fall for a floor plan.

- Water provider. Parts of San Tan Valley are served by private regulated water companies that have had rate and service cases in front of the Arizona Corporation Commission in recent years. Get the provider name for the address and read a recent bill if the seller will share one.

- Special districts and assessments. Some subdivisions carry community facilities district or similar assessments on top of county taxes. They can add real money per year and they do not always stand out in a listing summary. Pull the tax record for the parcel.

- Flood plain and washes. Desert washes run through and behind a lot of neighborhoods here. A lot that backs to a wash can be private and quiet, or it can carry flood insurance and drainage questions. Check the FEMA map and the seller disclosure, not the view.

- New construction competition. Builders are active in and around the valley now. A resale home competes with rate buydowns and closing cost incentives down the street. That affects buyers (negotiating room) and sellers (what you need to match).

## Selling in San Tan Valley

Your competition is not only the house two doors down. It is the builder model with an incentive sheet. We will price against both, look at what actually closed in your subdivision in the last 90 days, and decide what to fix and what to leave alone based on return, not opinion.

For current sales data, see the latest San Tan Valley & Florence market update. For town government and development news, follow San Tan Valley community news.

Common Questions

## Straight Answers About San Tan Valley

### What's the difference between Pecan Creek and Johnson Ranch?

Both are great communities, but they have a different feel. Pecan Creek tends to attract buyers looking for a quieter, more established neighborhood. Johnson Ranch has more amenities -- a golf course, multiple pools, and a stronger HOA presence. The right one depends on what you actually want in a neighborhood, and I've helped buyers choose between them enough times to walk you through it clearly.

### Is San Tan Valley a good place to buy right now?

In my opinion, yes -- but it depends on what you're looking for. San Tan Valley still offers more space for the money than most parts of the Phoenix metro. Inventory moves, and there are still deals if you know where to look. I won't oversell it -- there are some areas I'd steer you away from and others I'd point you toward. Call me and I'll give you a straight read on the current market.

### Do you only work in San Tan Valley, or other areas too?

San Tan Valley is my primary market, but I also specialize in Florence. Between those two, I cover a lot of ground -- residential homes, land parcels, new construction, and resale. If you're looking somewhere outside those areas, I'll be upfront about whether I'm the right fit or whether you'd be better served by someone with deeper local knowledge in that specific market.

## PAGE: Johnson Ranch (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/johnson-ranch

## Johnson Ranch

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Johnson Ranch

## The short version

Johnson Ranch is the community most people picture first when they say San Tan Valley. It is a roughly 2,000-acre master plan at Hunt Highway and Bella Vista Road, built out from the early 2000s, with an 18-hole public golf course running through it, three recreation centers, and commercial corners at Hunt Highway and Bella Vista so groceries and coffee do not require a trip to Queen Creek.

It is also where I live and work -- the Johnson Ranch area is home base for me. That cuts both ways for you as a buyer: I know which streets back to the wash, which villages sit closest to Hunt Highway noise, and where the golf course lots actually get a view. Ask me the specific question about a specific street.

## Quick facts

- Location: Hunt Highway at Bella Vista Road, San Tan Valley 85143

- Size: About 2,000 acres, roughly 6,100 homes planned at build-out across many villages

- Built: Late 1990s / early 2000s through today, village by village

- Golf: The Golf Club at Johnson Ranch, 18-hole championship course, par 72, about 7,100 yards

- Recreation: Lakeview, Indigo Sky, and Stardust recreation centers, each with a 25-meter pool and spa; Greens Park with a pitch-and-putt course and catch-and-release fishing lake; Twilight Park softball field; about 30 smaller pocket parks

- HOA: Yes. Amount and what it covers varies by village -- confirm for the specific home

- Schools: Florence Unified for most of Johnson Ranch (Walker Butte Middle School area, Poston Butte High School). Verify by address

## Homes and lots

Mostly one and two-story stucco homes with tile roofs, a lot of them with desert or low-water landscaping out front and block fencing behind. Sizes run from smaller starter floor plans around 1,200 square feet to golf course and larger family homes well over 3,000 square feet. Interior lots are the value play. Golf course frontage and mountain-view lots carry a premium and they resell differently -- a buyer for a fairway lot is buying the view as much as the house.

Watch for: age of roof underlayment and AC units on the earliest villages, and whether a home has had the original windows and water heater addressed. None of that is a reason to walk. It is a reason to price it correctly.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Johnson Ranch in the last 90 days.

## Parks and daily life

The three recreation centers are the practical center of the neighborhood: pools in summer, tennis and pickleball at Lakeview, basketball at Indigo Sky, and a calendar of classes and community events run through the HOA. Greens Park and the fishing lake get used more than people expect. Hunt Highway gives you Fry's, Walgreens, and a growing set of restaurants and services within the community's commercial corners.

San Tan Mountain Regional Park is a short drive west for hiking and mountain biking. Schnepf Farms and the Queen Creek Olive Mill are north in Queen Creek and are an easy weekend trip, not an everyday errand.

## Schools

Most Johnson Ranch addresses are Florence Unified School District: Walker Butte Middle School and Poston Butte High School are the schools commonly assigned, and the elementary school depends on the street. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

## Getting around

Hunt Highway is your main route north toward Queen Creek and the Loop 202 via Ironwood/Gantzel or via Queen Creek. Bella Vista connects east-west across the south valley. At commute and school hours, Hunt Highway and the Gantzel intersection slow down. If you work in Gilbert, Chandler, or Mesa, drive it at 7 a.m. once before you decide.

## Tradeoffs to know

- It is big. "Johnson Ranch" on a listing can mean a five-minute drive from one end to the other. Pin the actual street before comparing prices.

- HOA structure is village-based. Fees, amenities access, and rental rules are not identical across the whole master plan.

- Older villages need a closer look at roofs, AC, and plumbing than a 2018 build. Budget inspections accordingly.

- Golf course living has a window and patio reality: errant balls happen. Look at where the lot sits relative to the tee box and fairway, not just the view.

## Who Johnson Ranch Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who want amenities, golf, and services inside the neighborhood and who plan to use them; families who want middle and high school in the Florence Unified system nearby; sellers in the earlier villages who price against condition honestly.

### Look elsewhere if

You do not want an HOA at all (look at ranchette pockets), or you need the shortest possible commute to the 202 and price is secondary (start in Ironwood Crossing or Pecan Creek), or you want a gated 55-plus setup (look at Solera, inside this same master plan).

## Common Questions About Johnson Ranch

### Is Johnson Ranch in Queen Creek or San Tan Valley?

San Tan Valley. The postal address confuses people. It is in the Town of San Tan Valley, Pinal County, on Hunt Highway.

### Is the golf course private?

No. The Golf Club at Johnson Ranch is open to public play, with membership options. The Solera section inside Johnson Ranch has its own private clubhouse for Solera residents.

### Can I find a home without an HOA in Johnson Ranch?

No. Johnson Ranch is an HOA master plan. If no HOA is the priority, we look outside the master plans.

## PAGE: Solera at Johnson Ranch (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/solera-at-johnson-ranch

## Solera at Johnson Ranch (55-plus)

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Solera at Johnson Ranch

## The short version

Solera is the gated 55-plus Del Webb enclave inside the much larger, all-ages Johnson Ranch master plan. You get two layers: a private Solera clubhouse and pool for Solera residents, and access to the wider Johnson Ranch amenities and the 18-hole golf course that runs through the neighborhood. For a lot of buyers that is the right compromise -- a quieter, age-restricted street to come home to, without being cut off from grandkids, golf, and the recreation centers down the road.

## Quick facts

- Location: Inside Johnson Ranch, San Tan Valley 85143, off Hunt Highway / Bella Vista area

- Homes: 727 single-family homes, built 2004–2008 by Del Webb

- Type: Age-restricted 55-plus, gated (not guard-gated)

- Homes: Single-level, roughly 1,400–1,900 square feet, 2-car garages typical

- Clubhouse: About 10,000 square feet, private to Solera, with fitness center, pool and spa, ballroom, library, hobby and card rooms, bocce

- Golf: The Golf Club at Johnson Ranch winds through Solera. Golf is a separate cost from the HOA -- confirm current membership and play rates with the club

- HOA: Yes, Solera association plus Johnson Ranch master association -- confirm both amounts for the specific home

## Homes and lots

All single-level ranch plans. That matters as people age in place: no stairs, wider halls in most plans, and low-maintenance yards. Many homes back to the golf course or to open desert with San Tan Mountain views. The tradeoff of a 2004–2008 build is original systems. On any Solera purchase, look hard at roof underlayment condition, AC age, and water heater, and get a sewer line view if the inspector recommends it. Well-maintained Solera homes with those items already addressed sell differently than ones where they are all waiting for the next owner.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Solera at Johnson Ranch in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

The clubhouse runs the calendar: fitness classes, clubs, dances, day trips. Johnson Ranch's three recreation centers and Greens Park are available to you as a Johnson Ranch resident, and Hunt Highway commercial is minutes away for groceries and medical. Banner Ironwood Medical Center is on Combs Road. If family visits, they are not limited to the Solera pool rules the way they would be in a stand-alone 55-plus with no all-ages layer around it -- check current guest rules with the association before you promise the grandkids a pool day.

## Who Solera at Johnson Ranch Fits

### Good fit

Buyers 55-plus who want single-level living, a real clubhouse social calendar, and golf in the neighborhood, at a San Tan Valley price point; snowbirds who want a gated, low-maintenance home to lock and leave (confirm the association's exterior maintenance scope).

### Look elsewhere if

You want a brand-new 55-plus build with a large resort club (look at Trilogy at Encanterra or Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch in Florence), or you do not want two HOA layers, or nobody in the household meets the age restriction rules. At least one occupant must be 55-plus and there are limits on occupants under 19 -- get the current rules from the association, in writing, before you write.

## Common Questions About Solera at Johnson Ranch

### Can someone under 55 buy in Solera?

The community is operated for occupancy by persons 55 and older, with the usual federal and association rules on exceptions. Confirm the current occupancy rules with the Solera association for your specific household before you shop here.

### Is Solera gated and guarded?

Gated, not a 24-hour guard gate. Verify current gate access arrangements with the association.

### Do Solera residents use Johnson Ranch amenities?

Yes, Solera sits inside Johnson Ranch and residents have access to the master plan amenities in addition to the private Solera clubhouse. Confirm what the current master association includes.

## PAGE: Encanterra (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/encanterra

## Encanterra

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Encanterra

## The short version

Encanterra is the resort end of San Tan Valley. It is a gated Shea Homes community built around the La Casa club -- close to 60,000 square feet of dining, pools, spa, fitness and event space -- a second smaller club called The Algarve, and a private Tom Lehman-designed golf course. Part of the community is open to all ages and part is Trilogy, the 55-plus section. Everyone uses the same clubs.

This is not the least expensive way to live in San Tan Valley, and the community does not pretend otherwise. The question here is not price per square foot. It is whether you will actually use what the dues pay for.

## Quick facts

- Location: Combs Road east of Ironwood/Gantzel, San Tan Valley / Queen Creek postal area 85140

- Developer: Shea Homes. All-ages Encanterra plus Trilogy at Encanterra (55-plus)

- Clubs: La Casa (about 60,000 sq ft) and The Algarve (about 8,000 sq ft)

- Golf: Private 18-hole Tom Lehman championship course. Membership is separate from home ownership -- confirm current initiation and dues with the club

- Amenities: Multiple pools including indoor and adults-only options, Alvea Spa, four dining venues including Bistro 1528, athletic club, tennis, pickleball (8 courts at The Algarve), bocce, amphitheater, demonstration kitchen and artisan studio

- Homes: Single-level and some two-story plans roughly 1,300–3,500+ square feet depending on collection and section, new construction still active plus resales

- Gate: Gated community. Confirm current guard/gate arrangements with the association

## The two decisions inside Encanterra

First, section. The 55-plus Trilogy section and the all-ages section share clubs and golf, but the street you live on, the association rules, and who can occupy the home differ. Shea has at times sold new homes in the 55-plus section to buyers younger than 55 under builder policy. That policy belongs to the builder and the association and it changes. Do not rely on a blog post about it, including this one. We confirm it in writing for the specific home and section you are looking at.

Second, club economics. There is a mandatory social membership structure and an optional golf membership. Get both schedules of costs before you compare an Encanterra resale to a new build, because incentives, membership transfers, and what is included are not the same on both sides of that comparison.

## Homes

Shea builds to a higher finish level than most of the valley, with open plans, larger kitchens, and owners' suites designed for main-level living. Resales range from smaller lock-and-leave plans to golf course homes with casitas and pools. Because the community opened in the late 2000s, the earliest resales are at the age where roofs, AC systems, and pool equipment need a real inspection budget.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Encanterra in the last 90 days.

## Who Encanterra Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who want a private club life -- golf, spa, dining, clubs and classes -- without driving to Scottsdale to get it; 55-plus buyers who want a newer home and a large clubhouse; all-ages buyers who want a gated community with that same amenity base.

### Look elsewhere if

Club dues on top of an HOA do not fit the monthly budget you want to carry; you want no HOA or a rural lot; or you will not use the amenities. Paying for La Casa and never walking into it is the most common way buyers overspend in San Tan Valley.

## Common Questions About Encanterra

### Is Encanterra only 55-plus?

No. There is an all-ages section and a 55-plus Trilogy section inside the same gate. Confirm which section any specific home is in.

### Is the golf course public?

No. It is a private club course for members and their guests. Membership costs are separate from buying the home.

### Should I talk to an agent before visiting the sales office?

Yes. If new construction is part of your search, your right to your own representation is protected by registering correctly on the first visit. Call before you go, not after.

## PAGE: Pecan Creek (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/pecan-creek

## Pecan Creek (North and South)

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Pecan Creek

## The short version

Pecan Creek is where a lot of Queen Creek overflow landed, and it still works that way. It sits in the northern part of San Tan Valley, south of Ocotillo Road around Ironwood/Gantzel, split into Pecan Creek North and Pecan Creek South, with about 1,300 homes between them. The draw is straightforward: elementary schools inside the neighborhood, four main parks connected by walking paths, and a shorter drive to Queen Creek retail and the Loop 202 than most of San Tan Valley gets.

## Quick facts

- Location: South of Ocotillo Road, around Ironwood Drive / Gantzel, San Tan Valley 85140

- Homes: About 1,318 homes across North and South, built primarily in the 2000s boom

- Sizes: Roughly 1,290 to over 3,000 square feet, one and two-story

- Parks: Four main parks plus greenbelts, with playgrounds, basketball, volleyball, baseball/soccer fields and walking paths

- Schools: J.O. Combs Unified -- Jack W. Harmon Elementary (North) and Ellsworth Elementary (South) inside the community, J.O. Combs Middle School and Combs High School nearby

- HOA: Yes. Confirm dues and coverage for North vs South separately (they are not the same association experience)

## Homes and lots

Production homes from the 2000s: stucco, tile roofs, three to five bedrooms, a lot of two-story plans with the primary suite up or down depending on builder. The larger four and five-bedroom plans are a real part of this neighborhood's housing stock. Lots are typical subdivision size, not acreage. Homes that have been updated inside (kitchen, flooring, primary bath) separate quickly from original-condition homes in the same floor plan, and buyers pay for the done work here because so much of the competition needs it.

Inspection note for this era of build: original roof underlayment, AC age, and cast-iron or early plumbing details where applicable. Get the inspection. Price what it finds.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Pecan Creek in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

The parks are the amenity. There is no clubhouse and no community pool at Pecan Creek, which keeps HOA costs in a different class than Johnson Ranch or Ironwood Crossing. People use the parks, the greenbelts, and the schools' fields, and they drive to Queen Creek for the rest: Queen Creek Marketplace, the library, Horseshoe Park and Equestrian Centre, Schnepf Farms and the Olive Mill on weekends.

That tradeoff is the whole decision in Pecan Creek. Lower monthly carrying cost, more driving for entertainment and shopping.

## Schools

J.O. Combs Unified School District. Harmon Elementary serves the north side and Ellsworth Elementary the south, with Combs Middle School and Combs High School a short drive. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer. Charter options nearby include Legacy Traditional and American Leadership Academy campuses.

## Getting around

This is one of the better commute positions in San Tan Valley. Ironwood/Gantzel north to the Loop 202 and State Route 24, or Ocotillo west into Queen Creek and Chandler. It still slows at school hours -- Ellsworth and Gantzel is a known pinch -- but you start closer than the Hunt Highway neighborhoods do.

## Who Pecan Creek Fits

### Good fit

Families who want an elementary school they can walk to and a shorter Queen Creek commute; buyers who would rather have a larger floor plan than a community pool; sellers with an updated home, because original-condition competition is common here.

### Look elsewhere if

A community pool and clubhouse are must-haves (Ironwood Crossing, Johnson Ranch), or you want Florence Unified schools specifically, or you want a brand-new build (look at the active new construction around the valley and in Florence).

## Common Questions About Pecan Creek

### What is the difference between Pecan Creek North and South?

They are two phases of the same master community with separate elementary schools (Harmon in the north, Ellsworth in the south) and separate HOA details. The housing stock and the commute are similar. Compare the specific street and the specific association, not just the name.

### Does Pecan Creek have a community pool?

No clubhouse pool. The amenity base is parks, greenbelts and fields. If a pool matters, plan on a private pool home or a different neighborhood.

### Which district is Pecan Creek in?

J.O. Combs Unified, not Florence Unified. That distinction matters to a lot of families moving within San Tan Valley.

## PAGE: San Tan Heights (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/san-tan-heights

## San Tan Heights

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/San Tan Heights

## The short version

San Tan Heights is one of the largest communities in San Tan Valley, roughly 3,800 homes built into the foothills on the west side of the valley, with the San Tan Mountains in front of you and the Superstitions behind. People buy here for the views, the trails, and the space between houses compared to the tighter northern subdivisions. They accept a longer drive to do it.

This is Florence Unified territory, not J.O. Combs. Families moving from Pecan Creek or Ironwood Crossing sometimes miss that until they look up the high school. Check it at the start.

## Quick facts

- Location: West San Tan Valley, around San Tan Heights Boulevard and Thompson Road, 85142 (some listings show Queen Creek postal)

- Homes: About 3,800, from roughly 1,100 to over 3,500 square feet

- Community features: Multiple parks, playgrounds throughout the community, greenbelts, and 6-plus miles of paths and trails

- Schools: Florence Unified -- San Tan Heights Elementary inside the area; middle school assigned by address; San Tan Foothills High School. Verify by address

- HOA: Yes. Confirm current dues with the association. Community features listed in recent listings include pool, tennis, playgrounds, walking paths and fitness facilities through the association -- confirm what the current HOA covers, because marketing copy on this point is inconsistent

## Homes and lots

A mix of builders over a long build-out, including D.R. Horton and others, so floor plans and finish levels vary more street to street than in a single-builder community. Foothill lots can sit above the street behind them, which is where the mountain views come from and also where drainage and retaining questions need a closer look on inspection. View lots hold value differently here. A home that looks across the valley at sunset is not the same product as the same floor plan two streets down with a block wall view, and they should not be priced the same.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in San Tan Heights in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

The community parks and greenbelts are the everyday gathering points. San Tan Mountain Regional Park is effectively your backyard trail system -- more than 10,000 acres for hiking, biking and horses. Day to day, you will drive east to Hunt Highway or north to Queen Creek for most retail. San Tan Flat, the steakhouse and live music spot on Hunt Highway, is the local institution people actually name when you ask where they go.

## Schools

Florence Unified School District. San Tan Heights Elementary serves the community, with middle school assigned by address and San Tan Foothills High School as the path for older students. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer. American Leadership Academy has a San Tan campus in this part of the valley for families looking at charter options.

School closure watch: San Tan Heights Elementary appears on both of the closure recommendations that Florence Unified's school closure committee sent to the district in August 2026. Nothing has been decided, and a Governing Board vote is expected in December. Read the update.

## Getting around

Be honest with yourself about this one. You are on the west and south side of the valley. Queen Creek retail is reachable, the Loop 202 via Ironwood is a real drive, and there is no short freeway option yet. The tradeoff buys you views and space. Buyers who work from home or work in Florence or Coolidge are fine. Buyers commuting daily to Tempe or Scottsdale need to drive it at their commute time and decide with their eyes open.

## Who San Tan Heights Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who put mountain views and trail access ahead of commute minutes; Florence Unified families; buyers who want a larger community with a range of home sizes, including smaller lower-maintenance options.

### Look elsewhere if

Daily freeway commute time is your top priority (Pecan Creek, Ironwood Crossing), or you want a community pool and clubhouse as the center of the neighborhood (Johnson Ranch, Ironwood Crossing).

## Common Questions About San Tan Heights

### Which school district is San Tan Heights in?

Florence Unified. The high school path is San Tan Foothills, not Combs. Verify by address.

### Why do some San Tan Heights listings say Queen Creek?

Postal addresses and marketing areas overlap here. The parcel is in San Tan Valley. Check county records for the actual jurisdiction and tax record.

### Is there a community pool?

Association amenities have been described differently across sources. Confirm the current amenity list and HOA cost with the association for the specific home before relying on it.

## PAGE: Copper Basin (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/copper-basin

## Copper Basin

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Copper Basin

## The short version

Copper Basin was designed differently than most of San Tan Valley. Instead of a subdivision with a park in the middle, it was built around a village center on Main Street: a YMCA, an elementary school, a fire station, a church, and a 20-acre park, all inside the neighborhood. About 847 acres off Hunt Highway and Copper Mine Road. For families, that layout changes the daily routine. A lot of the week can happen without getting on Hunt Highway.

## Quick facts

- Location: Hunt Highway at Copper Mine Road / Drifter Pass area, San Tan Valley 85143

- Size: About 847 acres, D.R. Horton master developer, with later phases including Express Homes

- Center: Copper Basin YMCA with fitness center, rock wall, and zero-entry outdoor pool; Copper Basin Elementary; fire station; 20-acre park with playground, basketball courts and fields

- Homes: One and two-story, roughly 1,050 to over 3,700 square feet across the full build-out; newer phases cluster around 1,400–2,500 square feet

- HOA: Yes. Confirm current dues with the association. YMCA access terms for residents (pool use and membership discount) are a selling point here and they have been described in older marketing -- confirm the current resident terms with the YMCA and the association

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Copper Basin Elementary inside the community, Poston Butte High School nearby

## Homes

Copper Basin has been building for a long time, so there are two different purchases here. The earlier villages are 2000s and early 2010s homes where condition and updates decide the price. The later D.R. Horton phases are newer, more energy-efficient, and compete directly with new construction elsewhere in the valley and in Florence. Do not average them together when you price, either as a buyer or a seller.

The Main Street core holds value for a practical reason: proximity to the school, the Y, and the park is walkable in a way most of San Tan Valley is not. Homes deep in the later phases trade some of that walkability for newer construction.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Copper Basin in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

The YMCA is the social center -- youth sports, fitness classes, family programs, and the pool in summer. The 20-acre park handles the pickup games and the dog walking. Retail is a short drive north on Hunt Highway toward Johnson Ranch and Queen Creek. San Tan Mountain Regional Park is west for trails.

## Schools

Florence Unified School District, with Copper Basin Elementary inside the community, middle school assigned by address, and Poston Butte High School a few minutes away. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

School closure watch: Copper Basin Elementary appears on both of the closure recommendations that Florence Unified's school closure committee sent to the district in August 2026. Nothing has been decided, and a Governing Board vote is expected in December. Read the update.

## Getting around

You are in the southern half of San Tan Valley. Queen Creek and the Loop 202 are north on Hunt Highway and Ironwood/Gantzel. Florence is south, which makes Copper Basin a reasonable base for people who work in Florence or Coolidge, and a longer commute for people who work in the East Valley core. Drive your route at your time.

## Who Copper Basin Fits

### Good fit

Families who want the school, the Y, and the park inside the neighborhood; buyers who want a newer phase without going all the way to a brand-new Florence subdivision; sellers in the older villages who have done the kitchen and systems work buyers are screening for.

### Look elsewhere if

You want no HOA, or a private-club amenity level (Encanterra), or the shortest commute north (Ironwood Crossing, Pecan Creek).

## Common Questions About Copper Basin

### Do Copper Basin residents get to use the YMCA pool?

Resident YMCA terms have historically included pool access and a membership discount. Confirm the current terms -- this is exactly the kind of benefit that changes, and it should be verified, not assumed from an old flyer.

### Is Copper Basin in Florence schools if it sits that far south?

Yes. Copper Basin is Florence Unified, with its own elementary school inside the community.

### Newer phase or older village?

Newer gets you efficiency and warranty-era systems. Older gets you the Main Street location and usually a lower entry price. The right answer depends on the specific home's condition. We price both before you choose.

## PAGE: Ironwood Crossing (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/ironwood-crossing

## Ironwood Crossing

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Ironwood Crossing

## The short version

Ironwood Crossing is the amenity-heavy option in northern San Tan Valley. Built by Fulton Homes at Ironwood and Ocotillo, it has about 20 parks, an aquatics center with a splash pad and a heated pool of roughly 7,000 square feet that is open year-round, a clubhouse, and a charter school campus inside the community. It also has one of the better commute positions in the valley, up Ironwood to the Loop 202 and State Route 24.

Families choose between Ironwood Crossing and Pecan Creek a lot. The difference is simple: Ironwood Crossing charges more in HOA and gives you a pool, an aquatics center, and more programmed amenities in return. Pecan Creek charges less and gives you parks and schools. Decide which monthly bill matches how you actually live.

## Quick facts

- Location: Ironwood Drive and Ocotillo Road, San Tan Valley 85140

- Builder: Fulton Homes (original master developer)

- Amenities: Aquatics center with splash pad and heated pool, clubhouse with kitchen, about 20 parks with basketball courts, soccer fields, ramadas, barbecue areas and tot lots

- School inside: Legacy Traditional School -- Queen Creek campus (charter, grades K-6 at that campus) inside the community; district schools are J.O. Combs Unified

- Homes: Roughly 1,350 to over 4,000 square feet

- HOA: Yes, and it funds a real amenity base. Confirm current dues and what they include with the association (listings have shown water/trash bundled in some phases)

## Homes and lots

Fulton built a lot of family floor plans here: three to five bedrooms, a good number of them with a den or a loft, and larger lots than you find in some of the tighter northern subdivisions. Because the community has been built over many years, condition spreads widely. An original 2008 kitchen and a renovated 2023 kitchen in the same plan are different products and the sold data will show it.

Watch: pool equipment age on pool homes (a private pool on top of the community aquatics center is a choice, not a default need), and HOA transfer and amenity details at resale. Get the association documents early.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Ironwood Crossing in the last 90 days.

## Schools

District schools are J.O. Combs Unified: Ranch Elementary, J.O. Combs Middle School, and Combs High School are the schools commonly assigned. Legacy Traditional charter school operates a campus inside the community. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

## Getting around

Ironwood north is your freeway route, and Banner Ironwood Medical Center is about seven minutes away on Combs Road. Queen Creek Marketplace and the Queen Creek retail corridor are close. This is as good as the commute gets in San Tan Valley without living in Queen Creek itself. It is still a surface-street drive to the 202. Time it at your hour.

## Who Ironwood Crossing Fits

### Good fit

Families who will use a community pool and aquatics center weekly in summer and do not want to maintain a private pool; buyers who want a charter school option inside the neighborhood; sellers with a renovated home, because you are competing with a lot of original-condition listings.

### Look elsewhere if

The HOA amount bothers you more than the amenities are worth to you (Pecan Creek), or you want Florence Unified schools (most of southern San Tan Valley), or you want an acre lot with no HOA.

## Common Questions About Ironwood Crossing

### Is the Ironwood Crossing pool open year-round?

The community aquatics center pool is heated and has been marketed as year-round. Confirm current hours and season with the association.

### District school or charter?

Both exist here. The assigned district schools are J.O. Combs. Legacy Traditional's Queen Creek campus sits inside the community and enrolls by its own process. Families choose between them for program reasons, not distance.

### Does the HOA include water or trash?

Some listings have shown bundled services in certain phases. Do not assume it. Read the association resale documents for the specific home.

## PAGE: Circle Cross Ranch (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/circle-cross-ranch

## Circle Cross Ranch

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Circle Cross Ranch

## The short version

Circle Cross Ranch is a Pulte-built master community off Gantzel (Ironwood) and Empire Boulevard in the northern-central part of San Tan Valley. It has its own elementary school, a large central park -- Empire Park -- and a trail system that runs through the neighborhood. Of the Florence Unified communities in San Tan Valley, it is one of the closer ones to Queen Creek, Gilbert, and Mesa, which is why it lands on a lot of short lists for people who work north but want Florence Unified schools or a southern San Tan Valley price.

## Quick facts

- Location: Gantzel Road and Empire Boulevard area, San Tan Valley 85143

- Builder: Primarily Pulte Homes (built out; resale market now)

- Parks: Empire Park with basketball and volleyball courts, sports fields, picnic pavilions and playground; tot lots throughout; walking and biking trail network

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Circle Cross Ranch Elementary inside the community, Poston Butte High School minutes away

- Homes: Roughly 1,000 to over 3,500 square feet across the build-out, many in the 1,800–3,000 range, two to six bedrooms

- HOA: Yes. Confirm current dues and what they cover with the association

## Homes and lots

Because Circle Cross Ranch is built out, this is a resale-only search. That has an advantage: you can see how the neighborhood actually lives, not how a model home says it will. Streets are established, landscaping is mature, and you can tell a lot from a Saturday drive-through. The homes are mostly 2000s Pulte plans with stucco and tile, open family rooms, and a range from starter size to larger two-story family plans.

On inspection, age is the theme again: roof underlayment, AC systems, and water heaters in the earliest phases. The homes where an owner has already done those items are the cleanest negotiations in the neighborhood.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Circle Cross Ranch in the last 90 days.

## Schools

Florence Unified School District. Circle Cross Ranch Elementary is inside the community, middle school is assigned by address, and Poston Butte High School is a few minutes away on Gantzel. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

School closure watch: Circle Cross Ranch Elementary appears on one of the two closure recommendations that Florence Unified's school closure committee sent to the district in August 2026. Nothing has been decided, and a Governing Board vote is expected in December. Read the update.

## Getting around

Gantzel north to Combs, Ocotillo, and the Queen Creek and Gilbert retail corridors. The Loop 202 via Ironwood/Gantzel is your freeway run. Circle Cross Ranch starts closer to that run than Copper Basin or the Hunt Highway communities do, and farther than Ironwood Crossing. Banner Ironwood Medical Center is nearby on Combs Road.

## Daily life

Empire Park is the community's front yard: courts, fields, pavilions, and the events the HOA runs through the year. Trails connect the streets, and San Tan Mountain Regional Park is the weekend option to the west. Day-to-day shopping is north on Gantzel toward Queen Creek.

## Who Circle Cross Ranch Fits

### Good fit

Florence Unified families who want the elementary school in the neighborhood and a shorter northern commute than the rest of Florence Unified San Tan Valley; buyers who prefer a built-out, established neighborhood over a construction zone; sellers who have maintained systems, because buyers here are comparing condition closely.

### Look elsewhere if

You want a brand-new home (Florence new construction, or the active building elsewhere in the valley), a community pool and clubhouse (Ironwood Crossing, Johnson Ranch), or no HOA.

## Common Questions About Circle Cross Ranch

### Is Circle Cross Ranch still building?

No, it is effectively built out. Expect a resale purchase with established streets and mature landscaping.

### Which high school?

Poston Butte High School, Florence Unified, minutes away on Gantzel. Verify by address.

### Does it have a community pool?

The amenity base is parks, courts, fields and trails, not a clubhouse pool. If weekly community pool use is a requirement, look at Ironwood Crossing or Johnson Ranch.

## PAGE: Skyline Ranch (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/skyline-ranch

## Skyline Ranch

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Skyline Ranch

## The short version

Skyline Ranch sits at the base of the San Tan Mountains in southern San Tan Valley. It is a quieter, more open-feeling community than the northern subdivisions: earth-toned Mediterranean-style homes on sidewalk-lined streets, desert landscaping, and mountain views that you do not have to buy a premium lot to get. At the edge of it is Encanto Real, a gated enclave of custom homes on acre lots with horse privileges, which is a different purchase entirely and is covered separately below.

Living here means choosing the mountains over the freeway. People who buy in Skyline Ranch generally know that going in.

## Quick facts

- Location: Southern San Tan Valley near the San Tan Mountains, 85143, off Hunt Highway / Thompson and Skyline Drive area

- Homes: One and two-story, roughly 1,200 to 4,100 square feet, two to six bedrooms

- Community: Pocket parks, playgrounds, walking and biking paths, sports courts. No central clubhouse pool as the defining amenity

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Skyline Ranch Elementary serving the community, Poston Butte High School

- Nearby charter option: American Leadership Academy San Tan Valley campus in this part of the valley

- Enclave: Encanto Real -- gated, custom homes on about 1-acre lots, horse privileges. This is a low-volume custom segment, priced separately from the main subdivisions

## Homes and lots

The main Skyline Ranch subdivisions are production homes with stucco and tile, low-water front yards, and backyards that range from standard subdivision size to pool-sized lots. Views are the variable. Homes that face the San Tans or sit on the community's higher streets carry a premium that holds up in resale because the view cannot be built away.

Encanto Real is custom territory: larger homes, acre lots, room for horses, trailers, and shops. If that is what you want, we search it as its own market. There are very few sales in any given quarter, so pricing needs a wider look-back and a conversation about land value, not just cost per square foot.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Skyline Ranch in the last 90 days.

## Schools

Florence Unified School District, Skyline Ranch Elementary, middle school assigned by address, and Poston Butte High School for older students. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

School closure watch: Skyline Ranch Elementary appears on one of the two closure recommendations that Florence Unified's school closure committee sent to the district in August 2026. Nothing has been decided, and a Governing Board vote is expected in December. Read the update.

## Daily life and getting around

San Tan Mountain Regional Park is right there -- hiking, biking, and horse trails across more than 10,000 acres. San Tan Flat on Hunt Highway is the local gathering spot. For retail you will drive north toward Queen Creek and Gilbert, or south toward Florence. This is not a five-minute-errand neighborhood for most things. It is a come-home-to-quiet neighborhood.

If you commute to the East Valley core daily, drive it at your hour. If you work from home, work in Florence, or keep non-standard hours, the drive matters less and the setting matters more.

## Who Skyline Ranch Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who prioritize mountain views and trail access; buyers who want more house for the money than the northern valley offers and can absorb the drive; acre-lot and horse buyers in Encanto Real; sellers on view lots, because that premium is real and needs to be marketed to the right buyer pool.

### Look elsewhere if

Commute minutes are the top priority, you want a clubhouse pool community, or you need walkable retail.

## Common Questions About Skyline Ranch

### Is Skyline Ranch gated?

The main subdivisions are not. Encanto Real, the acre-lot custom enclave at the community's edge, is gated.

### Can I keep horses in Skyline Ranch?

Not in the main subdivisions. Horse privileges are in Encanto Real and in the ranchette pockets around southern San Tan Valley. Confirm zoning and CC&Rs for any specific lot.

### Which high school serves Skyline Ranch?

Poston Butte High School, Florence Unified. Verify by address.

## PAGE: Rancho Bella Vista (San Tan Valley) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/san-tan-valley/rancho-bella-vista

## Rancho Bella Vista (North and South)

San Tan Valley neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/San Tan Valley/Rancho Bella Vista

## The short version

Rancho Bella Vista is really two communities built in the 2000s in southern San Tan Valley. The original Rancho Bella Vista is at Hunt Highway and Bella Vista Road, about 936 homes started in 2003. Rancho Bella Vista South is at Gantzel and Bella Vista, about 591 homes built 2005–2009. Between them you are looking at roughly 1,500 homes of established, resale housing with farmland around the edges and mountain views that the newer, tighter subdivisions do not always get.

Neither has a clubhouse or a community pool. What they have is space, mature streets, and a monthly cost profile that runs lighter than the amenity-heavy communities. For a lot of buyers that trade is exactly right.

## Quick facts

- Location: Hunt Highway at Bella Vista Road (North/original) and Gantzel Boulevard at Bella Vista Road (South), San Tan Valley 85143

- Built: 2003–2009. Original builders include Hancock Homes and Meritage (Rancho Bella Vista) and Ryland and Richmond American (South)

- Homes: Rancho Bella Vista averages around 2,100 square feet; South runs roughly 1,860–2,867 square feet. Lots around 7,100 square feet in the original community

- Amenities: Tot lots, walking paths, large open areas, sport courts, green space. No community pool or clubhouse

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Skyline Ranch Elementary and Magma Ranch Elementary serve this area, Poston Butte High School. Verify by address, because the two communities do not feed identically

- HOA: Yes, both communities. Generally a lighter amenity scope -- confirm current dues for North vs South separately

School closure watch: Skyline Ranch Elementary, one of the schools serving this area, appears on one of the two closure recommendations that Florence Unified's school closure committee sent to the district in August 2026. Nothing has been decided, and a Governing Board vote is expected in December. Read the update.

## Homes and condition

These are 2003–2009 homes, which puts most of them at the point where the first roof underlayment cycle, AC replacement, and water heater are either done or due. That is the negotiation in Rancho Bella Vista. A home with a 2022 roof and a 2023 AC is a materially different purchase than the same floor plan with 2006 systems, even if the kitchens look similar in photos.

Interiors range from original to fully renovated. Because there is no new construction inside these two communities, your competition as a seller is the renovated resale down the street, not a builder model. That makes condition and pricing discipline pay off here more than in areas where a builder incentive is setting the ceiling.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Rancho Bella Vista in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

You will drive for most things: north on Hunt Highway or Gantzel to Johnson Ranch commercial and Queen Creek, or south to Florence. In exchange you get quiet streets, open sky, and farmland at the edges that keeps the area feeling less dense than northern San Tan Valley. San Tan Mountain Regional Park is west. Florence is close enough to be a real option for errands and events, which is not true for most of San Tan Valley.

## Who Rancho Bella Vista Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who want an established home with a lighter HOA profile and do not need a community pool; buyers who work in or near Florence or Coolidge; sellers who have done the systems work and want it credited in the price.

### Look elsewhere if

A community pool, clubhouse, or YMCA is a must-have (Copper Basin, Johnson Ranch, Ironwood Crossing), or you want a new build with a warranty (Florence new construction).

## Common Questions About Rancho Bella Vista

### Are Rancho Bella Vista and Rancho Bella Vista South the same HOA?

No. They are separate communities with separate associations. Confirm fees and rules for the specific community the home is in.

### Which elementary school serves my home?

This area is served by Skyline Ranch Elementary and Magma Ranch Elementary depending on the street. Verify the assigned school by address with Florence Unified before writing an offer.

### Why do listings here sometimes look less expensive than Johnson Ranch?

Different amenity base and different build years, plus no golf course frontage premium. Compare total monthly cost and condition, not list price alone.

## PAGE: Florence Neighborhoods — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence

## Florence, Arizona Neighborhoods

Three markets sharing one name • Merrill Ranch, historic Florence, and new construction

Neighborhoods/Florence

## Start here

Florence is the Pinal County seat, southeast of San Tan Valley on State Route 79, and it is really three different real estate markets sharing a name.

The first is historic Florence: the original town along Main Street, with adobe and territorial-era buildings, the 1891 Pinal County Courthouse, McFarland State Historic Park, and homes that range from historic properties to small established subdivisions and manufactured housing.

The second is Anthem at Merrill Ranch on the north side of town along Hunt Highway: a large master plan split between an all-ages section (Parkside) and a 55-plus section (Sun City Anthem), built around the Poston Butte Golf Club, a large community park, and Florence Hospital at its northeast edge.

The third is the growth corridor between them and west toward San Tan Valley, where builders are actively selling new homes now -- Magma Ranch, Magic Ranch, and a string of newer subdivisions along Arizona Farms Road and Hunt Highway. This is where a Florence buyer today is most likely to end up comparing a new build against a resale at Merrill Ranch.

Sellers in Florence need to hear the same thing clearly: new construction is your competition. Builder incentives, rate buydowns, and quick-move-in inventory set the terms a resale has to answer. We price with that sheet in front of us.

## Quick facts: Florence as a whole

- Location: About 60 miles southeast of Phoenix, on SR-79. Roughly 25 miles to Phoenix-Mesa Gateway Airport from the north side of town.

- County role: Pinal County seat. County government, the courthouse, and correctional facilities are major local employers. That employment base is a real part of the housing demand here and it does not move with Phoenix market cycles the way some of the valley's demand does.

- Main corridors: SR-79 (Pinal Parkway / Florence Boulevard) north-south, Hunt Highway from San Tan Valley into the Merrill Ranch area, Arizona Farms Road east-west.

- Schools: Florence Unified School District -- Florence High School, Florence Middle School, and Anthem, Florence, and Magma Ranch elementary schools, plus Poston Butte and San Tan Foothills high schools serving the northern Florence / southern San Tan Valley area. Verify by address.

- Medical: Florence Hospital near Merrill Ranch, Sun Life Family Health Center, plus Banner Ironwood in San Tan Valley to the north.

- Signature events: Country Thunder Arizona each April at Canyon Moon Ranch, the Florence Junior Parada rodeo and parade in late November, the Historic Home Tour in February, plus the town's Fright Fest, Hometown Holiday parade, and 4th of July Freedom Fest.

- Land: Florence has a real land and ranchette market beyond the subdivisions, including irrigated and desert parcels. Land here needs water, access, flood plain, and zoning diligence that a subdivision lot does not.

## The Florence-specific questions to ask on any purchase

- CFD or special assessment. Anthem at Merrill Ranch carries a community facilities district assessment on the tax bill that pays for community infrastructure. It is a meaningful annual number, it is separate from the HOA, and buyers miss it. Get the full tax record, including the CFD line, before you compare a Merrill Ranch home to a home outside the CFD.

- Builder incentives versus resale. If you are buying new, the incentive sheet changes monthly and the lot premium, release timing, and rate buydown structure matter more than the base price. If you are selling resale, that same sheet is what your buyer is comparing you against.

- SR-79 and Hunt Highway. Traffic into Florence is a two-lane-highway reality in places. Country Thunder weekend and rodeo weekend are not normal traffic. Drive your commute, and if a big event week matters to you, know the calendar.

- Water and utilities by address. Town of Florence water serves much of Florence. Newer and outlying areas can differ. Confirm provider, and for land, confirm legal and physical water access in writing.

- Flood plain. The Gila River and its washes shape the land market south and west of town. Flood maps and elevation certificates matter here in a way they do not in most subdivisions.

For current sales data, see the latest San Tan Valley & Florence market update. For town government and development news, follow Florence community news.

Common Questions

## Straight Answers About Florence

### Can I buy land in Florence, Arizona?

Yes -- and Florence is one of the few places near Phoenix where land still makes financial sense. Parcels range from residential lots to larger acreage, and they attract buyers looking to build, invest, or own land at a price point that's disappeared from closer-in markets. I know which parcels are worth pursuing and which ones have issues you'd only discover after the fact. Give me a call before you start looking on your own.

### What should I know before buying in Florence?

A few honest things: Florence is further from the metro core than San Tan Valley, so the commute matters if you're in the office regularly. The small-town atmosphere is real -- this isn't a place with walkable shopping and restaurant rows. But if you're working remotely, retiring, or just want space and value, those tradeoffs often feel worth it. I'll give you a clear picture of what to expect so there are no surprises after you've signed.

### Who helps with Florence AZ real estate?

I'm Brian Butler with eXp Realty (License #SA701819000) and Florence is one of my two specialty markets. I know what's available, what's priced right, and what to watch out for. Reach me at 480-810-9255 or Brian@thebutlerrealty.com. No pressure, no pitch -- just honest answers.

### Is Florence AZ a good place to buy a home?

For the right buyer, yes. Florence is a strong fit for remote workers, people relocating from higher cost-of-living areas, buyers seeking more land than the metro can offer, and those interested in land investment. It's not the right fit for everyone -- and I won't tell you it is just to make a sale. Let's have an honest conversation about your situation and whether Florence actually makes sense for you.

## PAGE: Anthem at Merrill Ranch — Parkside (Florence) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence/anthem-at-merrill-ranch-parkside

## Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Parkside (All Ages)

Florence neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/Florence/Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Parkside

## The short version

Merrill Ranch is the master plan that put modern Florence on the map for most buyers. It sits on the north side of Florence along Hunt Highway, and it is split in two: Sun City Anthem, the 55-plus section to the north, and Parkside, the all-ages section to the south. Parkside is the family side. It wraps around a large community park with sports fields, a fishing pond, a dog park, a splash pad and playgrounds, with the Poston Butte Golf Club running through the community and Florence Hospital at the northeast edge.

If you want a master plan in Florence with a real park, an active community calendar, and a golf course, this is the default starting point. Then we check the CFD.

## Quick facts

- Location: North Florence, Hunt Highway corridor, 85132

- Sections: Parkside (all ages) and Sun City Anthem (55-plus, separate page)

- Builders over time: Pulte, Meritage, D.R. Horton and others, multiple series including estate series lots

- Homes: Mostly 2000s through today, one and two-story, roughly 1,370 to over 2,700 square feet in current and recent series, stucco with tile roofs

- Amenities: Community center, outdoor pool with waterslides, fitness center, tennis, pickleball and volleyball courts, sports fields, fishing ponds, splash pad, playgrounds, dog park

- Golf: Poston Butte Golf Club, 18 holes, Troon-managed, Gary Panks design -- confirm pay-to-play and membership options with the club

- CFD: Yes. Anthem at Merrill Ranch carries a community facilities district assessment. Get the exact annual figure from the tax record for the specific parcel

- HOA: Yes. Confirm current dues, and which amenities your section's dues cover

## The CFD conversation

Do this before the tour, not after. Homes at Merrill Ranch carry a CFD assessment on the county tax bill in addition to regular property tax and the HOA. It pays for infrastructure that built the community. It can amount to a real monthly difference when you convert it, and it runs with the property for a defined term. Two homes at the same list price, one inside the CFD and one outside, do not cost the same to own. We pull the full tax record -- county tax, CFD, and any other special assessments -- for any Merrill Ranch home you are serious about, and we put it next to the HOA so you see total carrying cost on one page.

Sellers: your buyer will find the CFD. Price and present the home with the total cost understood, and be ready with what it pays for (the park, the infrastructure, the community you are selling). Surprises kill deals. The CFD does not have to.

## Homes

Parkside housing ranges from smaller single-level plans that work for first-time buyers and downsizers who do not want the 55-plus section, to two-story family homes and larger estate-series lots. Resale condition spreads widely -- early 2000s originals sit a few streets from homes built in the last few years. New construction has been active in and around Merrill Ranch in recent series, so a resale buyer should always ask what the builders are offering this month before deciding a resale is the better value.

## Schools

Florence Unified. Anthem Elementary serves the community, middle school is assigned by address, with Florence High School and Poston Butte High School as the high school options depending on address. School assignments change and are set by address -- verify the assigned schools for a specific home before you write an offer.

## Daily life

The park is genuinely large and genuinely used: fields, the pond, events, movies and community nights. Hunt Highway connects you north to San Tan Valley and Queen Creek without going through historic Florence. Dining in Florence itself is limited and local in character -- places residents name include Valentino's and the spots in historic downtown -- and most residents do bigger shopping runs to Queen Creek or Coolidge. Florence Hospital being at the edge of the community is a practical plus for a lot of households.

## Who Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Parkside Fits

### Good fit

Families who want a master plan park and pool without leaving Florence; buyers who value the golf course and the community calendar; sellers who present total cost honestly and have the condition to compete with new series nearby.

### Look elsewhere if

The CFD plus HOA total does not fit your budget (look at the newer non-CFD subdivisions, or at Florence Gardens for 55-plus); you want to be in the historic town itself; or you need a fast freeway commute (start in San Tan Valley).

## Common Questions About Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- Parkside

### What is the CFD at Merrill Ranch and how much is it?

It is a community facilities district assessment on the tax bill that repays infrastructure costs. The amount is set by parcel and declines over the district's term. I will not quote a number on a website because the wrong number costs you money -- we pull the tax record for the exact home.

### Is Parkside the same HOA as Sun City Anthem?

They are sections of one master plan with their own age rules and amenity details. Confirm what your section's dues include and what requires the other section's facilities.

### How far is Merrill Ranch from Queen Creek shopping?

A Hunt Highway drive north into San Tan Valley and Queen Creek. Time it from the specific home. It is closer than historic Florence, farther than San Tan Valley's northern neighborhoods.

## PAGE: Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch (Florence) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence/sun-city-anthem-merrill-ranch

## Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch (55-plus)

Florence neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/Florence/Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch

## The short version

Sun City Anthem is the 55-plus northern section of the Merrill Ranch master plan in Florence. It has its own large private clubhouse for Sun City residents, and it also sits inside the larger Merrill Ranch community, so residents use the master plan's park, lakes, sports courts and water amenities as well. The Poston Butte Golf Club winds through the community. For 55-plus buyers who want a big-clubhouse lifestyle at a Florence price instead of a Queen Creek or Mesa price, this is usually the first community to look at in this part of Pinal County.

## Quick facts

- Location: North Florence, Merrill Ranch, off Hunt Highway / Anthem Way, 85132

- Type: Age-restricted 55-plus section within the all-ages Merrill Ranch master plan

- Clubhouse: About 48,000 square feet, private to Sun City -- fitness center, indoor and outdoor pools, restaurant and cafe, ballroom, hobby and game rooms

- Golf: Poston Butte Golf Club, 18-hole, about 7,300 yards, Gary Panks design, Troon-managed. Island-green par-3 is the hole people remember. Golf cost is separate from the HOA -- confirm current rates with the club

- Sports: Tennis, pickleball, bocce, horseshoes, plus Merrill Ranch basketball, sand volleyball, rock climbing wall and water park amenities in the wider community

- Homes: Single-level ranch-style plans in the Sun City section; one and two-story homes are in Parkside, the all-ages section

- CFD and HOA: Both apply. The Merrill Ranch CFD assessment is on the tax bill and association dues apply -- confirm both by parcel. This is the most important cost check in this community

## Homes

Sun City Anthem homes are single-level plans designed for main-level living, stucco and tile roofs, with a lot of golf course and mountain-view lots in the mix. Views toward Poston Butte and the desert are a real feature here on clear days. Build years run through the 2000s and 2010s with continued series after, so condition and updates drive the resale spread more than floor plan alone.

As with any 55-plus purchase, confirm the age-restriction compliance paperwork and the association's occupancy rules early, including guest and caregiver provisions and any limits on occupants under the age threshold. Get it from the association, in writing.

Current prices: Prices here move with the market, so this page does not post a number that will be out of date next month. Call or text 480-810-9255 and I will send you what has actually closed in Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch in the last 90 days.

## Daily life

The clubhouse calendar is the lifestyle: clubs, classes, trivia, dances, and seasonal events, plus the restaurant so dinner does not require leaving the community. Florence Hospital is at the northeast edge of Merrill Ranch, Hunt Highway takes you north to San Tan Valley and Queen Creek, and historic Florence is a short drive south for the library, the courthouse area, and town events like the Historic Home Tour and the Junior Parada.

For a lot of buyers the comparison set is Solera at Johnson Ranch (smaller, inside an all-ages golf community, San Tan Valley) and Trilogy at Encanterra (newer, private club, higher dues). Sun City Anthem tends to win on clubhouse scale and price for the size of home. It tends to lose on distance to the East Valley. Decide which of those matters more in your actual week.

## Who Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch Fits

### Good fit

55-plus buyers who want a large clubhouse and a full social calendar, golf in the community, and a single-level home; buyers relocating to be near adult children in San Tan Valley or Queen Creek who want their own 55-plus base 20 minutes away instead of in the same subdivision.

### Look elsewhere if

Total carrying cost with CFD and HOA does not fit; you want a brand-new 55-plus build (Trilogy at Encanterra, with a different dues structure); or you want to be inside the East Valley for daily family and medical routines (Solera at Johnson Ranch shortens that drive).

## Common Questions About Sun City Anthem at Merrill Ranch

### Is Sun City Anthem the same as Anthem at Merrill Ranch?

Sun City Anthem is the 55-plus section of the Anthem at Merrill Ranch master plan. Parkside is the all-ages section. Same master plan, different sections, different occupancy rules.

### Do I pay for golf with my HOA?

No. Golf at Poston Butte is separate. The HOA and CFD cover association and district costs. Confirm current club rates directly.

### Can family stay with me or move in?

Age-restricted occupancy rules apply. Confirm the current rules with the association for your household before you buy, including long-term guests and occupants under 55.

## Related Neighborhoods

Anthem at Merrill Ranch -- ParksideFlorence ->Solera at Johnson RanchSan Tan Valley ->EncanterraSan Tan Valley ->

55-plus plus a CFD plus a golf club is three sets of numbers. Call or text 480-810-9255 and we will stack them on one page before you decide if this community fits the budget you actually want to carry.
