## PAGE: Florence Gardens (Florence) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence/florence-gardens

## Florence Gardens (55-plus)

Florence neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/Florence/Florence Gardens

## The short version

Florence Gardens is the value end of 55-plus living in Florence, and the reason is in one sentence: you own the land. This is an established 55-plus community of ground-set manufactured homes on about 1,219 privately owned lots. There is no lot rent. There is a homeowner association with a comparatively low annual fee, a clubhouse, pools, and a full activity calendar. For retirees who want to own their lot, keep monthly costs down, and still have people and things to do, Florence Gardens has been the answer in Florence for a long time.

It is a different product than Sun City Anthem. Neither is better in the abstract. They are different monthly bills and different houses.

## Quick facts

- Location: Florence, accessed from SR-79 / Florence Boulevard toward Gila Boulevard and Cochise area, 85132

- Type: 55-plus active adult, manufactured homes on owned lots

- Lots: About 1,219 privately owned lots, roughly 60 by 100 feet (about 0.14 acre) typical

- Association: Homeowner-run board. Annual HOA fee has been listed in recent sales at a level far below the master plans -- confirm the current amount and what it includes

- Amenities: Clubhouse with auditorium and social events, annex with library and card rooms, two pools and spas, fitness room, pickleball courts, shuffleboard, billiards, horseshoe pits, wood carving and lapidary, and a 9-hole executive golf course (pay to play)

- Homes: Manufactured homes from older models through recent placements, including newer Cavco and similar homes on owned lots. Lot-and-a-half and golf course lots appear

## What to check, because this is not a standard subdivision purchase

- Land ownership versus lot rent is the headline, and it is the genuine advantage here. Confirm it on the title report for the specific lot anyway. Habits from other manufactured home communities will make you ask, and the answer here is the selling point.

- Manufactured home lending and insurance are different from site-built lending and insurance. Loan type, age of the home, foundation certification, and whether the home is titled as real property all affect your options and your rate. This conversation needs to happen with a lender who does manufactured housing in Arizona before you write an offer, not during escrow.

- Age of home and systems. A 1990s home and a 2017 or newer placement in Florence Gardens are different purchases at different insurance and lending terms, whatever the list price says. Get the HUD label data, the roof and AC ages, and the foundation details early.

- Resale reality. The buyer pool for a manufactured home on owned land is smaller than for a site-built home, and appraisal comparables stay inside the community. That cuts both ways: entry price is lower, and selling takes the right buyer and the right lender. Price it with Florence Gardens closed sales, not with Sun City Anthem.

## Daily life

The calendar here is resident-run and full: bingo, dances, social meals and holiday dinners, coffee socials, clubs for most hobbies, seasonal entertainment, and the golf course in the middle of it. It is an established community where people know each other, and where a lot of residents are seasonal. Ask about summer, not just the winter season, if you plan to live here year-round. Historic Florence is minutes away for the library, town events, and Main Street. Coolidge is the grocery run for many residents.

## Who Florence Gardens Fits

### Good fit

55-plus buyers who want to own their land, keep monthly costs low, and have an active clubhouse life without master plan dues; cash and well-prepared buyers who understand manufactured home financing before they shop; sellers who price inside the community's own sold data and have their title and foundation paperwork in order.

### Look elsewhere if

You need conventional site-built construction for your loan program or your own comfort (Sun City Anthem), you want a new build with a warranty, or you are not willing to do the extra lending and insurance diligence that a manufactured home requires.

## Common Questions About Florence Gardens

### Do I own the land in Florence Gardens?

Yes. Lots are privately owned and there is no lot rent. Confirm on the preliminary title report for the specific property, as you should with any purchase.

### Can I get a loan on a home in Florence Gardens?

Many buyers do, but terms depend on the age and type of the home and how it is titled. Talk to a lender experienced with Arizona manufactured housing before you make an offer.

### How does Florence Gardens compare to Sun City Anthem?

Owned land and a low annual association fee with a resident-run clubhouse, versus a larger master plan clubhouse, site-built homes, an HOA plus a CFD assessment. The monthly totals are not close, and neither are the houses. Compare total cost and the home itself, in that order.

## Related Neighborhoods

## PAGE: Historic Downtown Florence (Florence) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence/historic-downtown-florence

## Historic Downtown Florence

Florence neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/Florence/Historic Downtown Florence

## The short version

Downtown Florence is the original town, and it does not look or live like the subdivisions north of it. Main Street runs past the second Pinal County Courthouse from 1891, McFarland State Historic Park in the first courthouse from 1878, the Florence Community Library, town hall, and a small set of local restaurants and shops. Around it are the town's oldest neighborhoods: historic adobe and territorial-era homes in and near the historic district, post-war and later homes in the original town subdivisions, and -- a few streets away -- established manufactured home areas including Florence Gardens.

People buy in historic Florence because they want to live in a town with a past they can walk through, and because the entry price for a home in town can be lower than the master plans. They give up new construction, big amenities, and in some streets, the certainty that every neighboring home is maintained the same way an HOA would require.

## Quick facts

- Location: Main Street corridor, Florence 85132, around Ruggles Street and the courthouse

- Landmarks: First Pinal County Courthouse / McFarland State Historic Park (1878, jail added 1882, at Main and Ruggles), Second Pinal County Courthouse (1891), Florence Community Library at 778 N. Main Street, Pinal County Historical Society museum

- Housing stock: Historic Sonoran and territorial-style homes (some on the National Register), mid-century and later site-built homes in town subdivisions (listings reference areas such as Florence 70 and other original town plats), and manufactured housing areas nearby

- HOA: Many in-town homes have no HOA or a minimal one -- confirm by property. That is part of the appeal and part of the diligence

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Florence Elementary, Florence Middle School, and Florence High School in town

- Events base: This is where the town's calendar lives. Historic Home Tour in February, Junior Parada parade on Main Street in late November, Hometown Holiday lighting and parade in December, Fright Fest on Halloween, and town events through the year

## Buying a historic or older in-town home -- what changes

- Systems and structure diligence goes up. Adobe and older construction need an inspector who knows them: roof structure and drainage, foundation movement, older plumbing and electrical, and evaporative-to-refrigerated air conversions. Budget for the inspection and for the work it finds. None of it is a reason to avoid these homes. All of it is a reason not to price one like a 2015 subdivision home.

- Historic district rules. If the home is in the historic district or is a contributing property, exterior changes can require review. Confirm with the Town of Florence before you plan an addition, a wall, or a roofline change.

- Insurance and lending. Older homes and manufactured homes can carry different insurance costs and loan conditions. Quote both before you are in escrow.

- Land and lots. In-town Florence has vacant lots and small parcels that come up near the subdivisions. Check zoning, flood plain, utility taps (water and sewer at the lot versus a tap fee away), and whether the street is town-maintained.

## Daily life

You can walk more of your life here than anywhere else in Florence: library, town hall, courthouse events, Main Street restaurants, the senior center. The Dorothy Nolan Senior Center runs daily activities, a Wednesday biscuits and gravy breakfast, and Friday home-style lunches that are open community fixtures, not just senior programming. Coolidge, about 15 minutes south, handles the larger grocery and Walmart runs. Queen Creek and San Tan Valley are north on SR-79 and Hunt Highway when you need them.

What you will not find: a master plan pool, a golf course in the neighborhood, or a builder model to compare against. In-town Florence is for people who prefer a town to a community amenity package.

## Who Historic Downtown Florence Fits

### Good fit

Buyers who want character, history, and a walkable town core; buyers priced out of the master plans who would rather put money into an older home they can improve over time; county and town employees who want a short commute; sellers of well-kept in-town homes, because renovated historic and in-town homes are scarce compared to subdivision resales.

### Look elsewhere if

You want new construction and a warranty (the corridor west and north of town), a clubhouse and golf lifestyle (Merrill Ranch), or strict HOA-maintained uniformity on every street.

## Common Questions About Historic Downtown Florence

### Are there rules on changing a historic home's exterior?

If the property is in the historic district, exterior work can require town review. Confirm the property's status and the rules with the Town of Florence before planning changes.

### Is downtown Florence in an HOA?

Many in-town homes are not in an HOA. Verify for the specific property, and if no HOA matters to you, that freedom also means no HOA enforcement on neighboring properties.

### What is McFarland State Historic Park?

The preserved first Pinal County Courthouse from the territorial period at Main and Ruggles, now a state historic park with the restored courtroom and exhibits. It is the front door to Florence's history and the starting point for walking tours of the historic district.

## Related Neighborhoods

If a historic or in-town Florence home has your attention, call or text 480-810-9255. These purchases reward an inspector and a title search done right, and we will line both up before the offer.

## PAGE: Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor (Florence) — https://thebutlerrealty.com/neighborhoods/florence/magma-ranch-and-new-construction-corridor

## Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor

Florence neighborhood guide • Homes, schools, daily life, and the tradeoffs

Neighborhoods/Florence/Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor

## The short version

Most of the Florence home search in 2026 runs through new construction, and most of it sits west and northwest of historic Florence: Magma Ranch and its newer Magma Ranch Vistas series near San Tan Valley, Magic Ranch (including Oasis at Magic Ranch), and a set of active builder subdivisions along Arizona Farms Road and the Hunt Highway corridor. D.R. Horton, Starlight Homes, Meritage, Pulte, LGI, and Century Communities have all been active in Florence in recent series.

These neighborhoods compete on a simple offer: a new home, a warranty, and an incentive sheet, at a base price that undercuts a comparable resale in Queen Creek or Gilbert. The diligence is in the details the base price leaves out.

## Quick facts

- Area: West and northwest Florence, flowing into southern San Tan Valley along Arizona Farms Road and Hunt Highway, 85132

- Named communities to know: Magma Ranch, Magma Ranch Vistas (newer series), Magic Ranch and Oasis at Magic Ranch, plus active builder subdivisions such as Western Crossings and Bisbee Ranch in recent Florence releases. Builders open and close series quickly, so ask which communities are actively selling this month

- Homes: Current series are commonly 3–5 bedrooms, roughly 1,100–3,100 square feet depending on builder and plan, one and two-story, stucco and tile

- Amenities (Magma Ranch area): Community pool, clubhouse, fitness center, basketball courts, parks, trails and playgrounds in the Magma Ranch plan. Confirm the current amenity list by community, because Vistas and later phases do not always share the original list

- Schools: Florence Unified -- Magma Ranch Elementary serves this corridor, Florence High School for older students. Verify by address

- HOA: Yes. Confirm dues by community and phase. Ask about CFD or special assessments at the same time

## How to buy new construction here without overpaying

- Register correctly on the first visit. If you want your own representation, we need to be attached to the purchase from the first sales office visit. Call before you tour a model, not after you have a favorite lot.

- Compare total price, not base price. Lot premium, structural options, design studio selections, and the incentive structure (rate buydown versus price reduction versus closing costs) decide what the home actually costs. A lower base price with a large lot premium down a wash-facing street is not the same deal as it looks on the flyer.

- Ask what phase you are buying into. Early phase in a community that will build for years means construction traffic and unfinished amenities for a while, in exchange for the lowest entry price the community will likely offer. Later phases cost more and live better on day one. Neither is wrong. Know which you chose.

- Read the public report and the HOA budget. Arizona new-home purchases come with a subdivision public report. Read the sections on assessments, amenities timing, and who controls the association and until when.

- Get your own inspection, including a pre-drywall inspection if timing allows. A warranty is not an inspection, and builder walk-throughs are not a substitute for your own inspector on a new build. This is even more true on quick-move-in homes that were finished before you arrived.

## Resale competition note for sellers near this corridor

If you own a resale home in Florence or southern San Tan Valley, these incentive sheets are your competition. Before we list, we pull the current builder offers in the communities your buyer will cross-shop, and we price and present your home against them with condition and lot advantages stated in numbers.

## Daily life

You will do most shopping north in San Tan Valley and Queen Creek, or south in Florence and Coolidge. Magma Ranch's own pool and park handle a lot of the week for families. San Tan Mountain Regional Park and the Florence events calendar (Country Thunder in April, Junior Parada in November, the Historic Home Tour in February) are the local calendar anchors. SR-79 is your Phoenix route. Drive it at your commute time, including on a Friday, before you commit.

## Who Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor Fits

### Good fit

First-time and move-up buyers who want a new home and a warranty at a Florence price point; buyers who qualify well and can use a builder rate buydown effectively; VA and FHA buyers, who are a large part of this corridor's market and should have the incentive sheet priced into the comparison from the start.

### Look elsewhere if

You want an established neighborhood with mature landscaping and no construction (Merrill Ranch resales, Rancho Bella Vista in San Tan Valley); you want land and no HOA; or build timing and phase uncertainty do not fit your move date.

## Common Questions About Magma Ranch and the New Construction Corridor

### Should I visit the model homes first and call an agent later?

No. Your right to your own representation on a new build is established at registration on the first visit. Call or text me before the first model tour.

### Are incentives real or already in the price?

Both structures exist. The only honest way to know is to price the same plan, same lot type, with and without the incentive, and compare total cost and monthly payment. We do that in writing before you sign.

### Is Magma Ranch in Florence or San Tan Valley?

Florence, in the corridor that flows into southern San Tan Valley. The communities sit close enough that residents use both towns. The parcel's jurisdiction, school assignment, and tax record are Florence / Florence Unified -- verify by address for the specific community.

## Related Neighborhoods

New construction is where buyers leave the most money on the table in Florence, usually in the options and the incentive structure, not the base price. Call or text 480-810-9255 before your first model visit and we will price it properly from the start.
